claims.claim: GPT-style transformers trained on uniform random data show an empirical memorization-capacity plateau of about 3.6 bits per parameter (Figure 1)
claims.evidence: Tiny CPU GPT-style models were trained on seeded uniform random token data. The measured bits-per-parameter values are toy-scale observations and are not the paper-reported 3.6 bits-per-parameter plateau.

claims.claim: Capacity estimates across model widths and depths support a roughly linear bits-per-parameter scaling law, with bfloat16 to float32 increasing capacity only modestly (Table 1)
claims.evidence: The run compares tiny model sizes under the same seeded random-data protocol. Precision effects are not reproduced because deterministic CPU bfloat16 training was not used.

provenance.seed_policy: Python random and torch manual seeds are fixed per run.

title: How much can language models memorize?
